title: Finite-extension p-power intersection
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $K$ a field of characteristic $p$, $K^p=\{x^p:x\in K\}$, and $(K_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ a family of subfields of $K$ such that $K^p\subseteq K_\alpha$ for every $\alpha$, $\bigcap_\alpha K_\alpha=K^p$, and for every $\alpha,\beta$ some $\gamma$ satisfies $K_\gamma\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\beta$. The index set may be empty. Then for every finite field extension $L/K$ [def-pc-field-extension], $L^p=\bigcap_\alpha L^pK_\alpha$, where $L^p=\{x^p:x\in L\}$ and $L^pK_\alpha$ is the subfield of $L$ generated by $L^p$ and the image of $K_\alpha$.

proof.text: If the index type is empty, the intersection hypothesis says K^p=K. Thus Frobenius is surjective on K, giving PerfectRing K p and PerfectField K. A finite extension is algebraic, so Mathlib Algebra.IsAlgebraic.perfectField gives PerfectField L, and PerfectRing.bijective_frobenius gives L^p=L. This proves the equality with the empty intersection directly. These are the perfect-field results of Mathlib.FieldTheory.Perfect, used directly in the Lean proof.

proof.text: For a nonempty index type, choose the finite K-basis e=Module.finBasis K L and set b_i=e_i^p. Applying Frobenius to the basis expansion proves that L^p consists exactly of sums sum a_i b_i with a_i in K^p. Such sums are independent over K^p: choose p-th roots c_i in K; a zero sum is (sum c_i e_i)^p=0, so Frobenius injectivity and the original basis independence give c_i=0, hence a_i=0. Both facts are proved directly in the importing module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-frobenius-basis-compositum] to identify L^p K_alpha with the K_alpha-span of the b_i; no independence over K_alpha is assumed.

source.place: Tags 07P4 (lemma-intersection-subfields), proof of (2), and 07P3 (lemma-intersection-subfields-subspace); homogeneous coefficient descent instead of degree induction

proof.text: Let x belong to every L^p K_alpha. View F=K^p as the concrete subfield (frobenius K p).fieldRange and extend the scalar base of K_alpha to F. Their infimum is bottom by the intersection hypothesis and they remain downward directed. In K^(n+1), take the kernel of the K-linear map (a_1,...,a_n,t) to sum a_i b_i-t x (the Lean proof puts t in coordinate zero). For each alpha, the coefficient description provides a nonzero vector in this kernel with coordinates in K_alpha and t=1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-intersection-subfields-subspace] to obtain a nonzero kernel vector with every coordinate in K^p.

source.place: Tags 07P4 (lemma-intersection-subfields), proof of (2), and 07P3 (lemma-intersection-subfields-subspace); homogeneous coefficient descent instead of degree induction

proof.text: For this vector t cannot vanish: otherwise independence of the b_i over K^p, proved in Step 2, would make all a_i zero as well, contradicting nonzeroness. Divide its coefficients by t; since K^p is a subfield, the quotients still lie in K^p, and the kernel equation gives x=sum (a_i/t)b_i. The power-span characterization in Step 2 gives x in L^p. The opposite containment follows from the generators of each subfield closure. This completes the set equality without an induction on extension degree.

lean.statement: theorem intersection_subfields_differentials_powers (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (K : Type u) [Field K] [CharP K p] {ι : Type v} (Kα : ι → IntermediateField (ZMod p) K) (h₁ : ∀ α : ι, Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) ⊆ (Kα α : Set K)) (h₂ : Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) = ((⨅ α, Kα α : IntermediateField (ZMod p) K) : Set K)) (h₃ : ∀ α β : ι, ∃ γ : ι, Kα γ ≤ Kα α ⊓ Kα β) : ∀ (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L], Set.range (fun x : L => x ^ p) = ⋂ α : ι, ((Subfield.closure (Set.range (fun x : L => x ^ p) ∪ (algebraMap K L '' (Kα α : Set K))) : Set L))

mathlib_searches.query: Downward directed intermediate fields with Frobenius image as infimum detect zero Kahler differentials and preserve that infimum after finite field extension
In prime characteristic the intersection of a downward directed family of fields containing all pth powers detects Kahler differentials and commutes with finite extensions after adjoining pth powers
